Definition: to laugh (in pleasure or detraction); by implication, to play
BiblicalUsage: The word sâchaq means to laugh (in pleasure or detraction); by implication, to play. It stands in 1 Chronicles 13:8, "And David and all Israel played before God…", and in 1 Samuel 18:7, "…slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God put sâchaq here on purpose, and I take his word for it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
